extracted.intended_audience: CVPR 2019 reviewers / members of the CVPR 2019 Reviewing Committee
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewing submitted papers to CVPR 2019: how to evaluate technical content, write constructive reviews, follow ethical/conflict rules, and use the CMT reviewing system through preliminary rating, rebuttal, discussion, and final recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blind review and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors were asked to take reasonable efforts to hide their identities; reviewers should also make all efforts to keep their identity invisible to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not search for the authors of a paper, and do not complain that the paper is not anonymous if you happen to find them. Treat papers fairly whether or not you know (or suspect) who wrote them. See Author Guidelines for how authors preserve anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: ArXiv handling (not prior work)
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv papers are not considered prior work since they have not been peer reviewed; review CVPR papers independently as if the ArXiv papers didn't exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is NOT OK to: suggest rejection for not citing an arXiv paper; accept a paper solely because it performs better than something on arXiv; reject solely because it performs worse than something on arXiv; regard arXiv as the standard for state of the art. It is OK to: suggest an author should acknowledge something on arXiv; an author may decline to acknowledge it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for conflicts and comfort to review
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you get your reviewing assignment, go through all the papers to make sure there is no obvious conflict and that you feel comfortable reviewing the paper assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is a conflict (e.g., recent collaborator, same institution) or you are not comfortable, email the Program Chairs immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary evaluation criteria: novelty, potential impact, technical soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: CVPR looks for new ideas; each accepted paper should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace novel, brave concepts even if they have not been tested on many datasets. Do not base acceptance/rejection solely on raw performance; weigh novelty and potential impact alongside reported performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific: cite concrete related work and explain comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific and detailed in reviews; generic statements like 'this is well known' are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific publications, books, or public disclosures. When claiming prior work exists, back it up with specific references and explain how closely related they are.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write strengths and weaknesses as the main critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Main critique should be a list of strengths and weaknesses, using bullet points and explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain your arguments; include specific feedback on ways authors can improve. Discussion helps authors, fellow reviewers, and Area Chairs understand the basis of your opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inventing ad-hoc policy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not reject or penalize a paper for violations of policies that CVPR does not have; avoid ad-hoc policy innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rejecting a paper because its dataset is not public is unfair if CVPR has no policy requiring public datasets. If the issue is a conference policy (e.g., dual submission), follow stated policy; otherwise don't invent requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal scope: no new experiments requested or required
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not request additional experiments for the rebuttal, nor penalize papers for lack of additional experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not include new experimental results in the rebuttal; reviewers should discount any new results when making their final recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destroy materials after review
rubrics_metrics.description: After the review process, reviewers should destroy all copies of papers and supplementary material and erase any implementations and results used to evaluate the ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of confidentiality and ethics obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: be diplomatic, courteous, and constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone of the review is important; harshly written reviews will be disregarded even if criticisms are true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write diplomatically while staying true to your assessment. Put yourself in mindset of helping a respected colleague. Avoid belittling or sarcastic comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write thoughtful, detailed reviews (avoid short reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short reviews are unhelpful to authors, other reviewers, and Area Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you agreed to review, take enough time to write a thorough review. Read the paper and think about it over several days before writing your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable and specific writing feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific when you suggest the writing needs improvement; point out particular sections and give suggestions for clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which section is unclear and propose how to improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requesting authors to cite your own papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't give away your identity by asking the authors to cite several of your own papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to cite your work can reveal reviewer identity and are inappropriate unless fully justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate claims that work has been done before
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that submitted work 'has been done before' must be backed up with specific references and an explanation of how closely they are related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For positive reviews, summarize what novel aspects are most interesting among the paper's strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling out-of-scope submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is out of scope for CVPR's subject areas, clearly explain why in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Call for Papers and suggest other publication possibilities (journals, conferences, workshops) that would be a better match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use impersonal phrasing (avoid 'you')
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid referring to the authors directly using 'you'; use 'the authors' or 'the paper' instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using 'you' can be perceived as confrontational; impersonal phrasing is more professional and less inflammatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive suggestions for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Be generous in giving authors new ideas for improving the work, which may be specific or more general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest new datasets, application areas, numerical solvers, or ways the idea can be generalized. Helpful reviews benefit both authors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect confidentiality of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect confidentiality of ideas in submitted papers: do not show the paper or supplementary material to non-reviewers or use ideas from the paper to develop new work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should not show the paper to anyone (unless asked to help review), not show results/videos to non-reviewers, not use ideas for your own projects, and must destroy copies and erase implementations after the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid any conflict of interest; if assigned a paper where your review would create a possible conflict, return the paper and do not submit a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of conflicts include: same institution as an author; direct involvement in the work; collaboration within past three years; being an MS/PhD advisor or advisee; situations others might consider a conflict. Email Program Chairs if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional: avoid belittling or sarcastic comments and write courteous, informative, incisive, and helpful reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to write a review you would be proud to add your name to (if it were not anonymous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: When downloading assigned papers, check for conflicts and submission rule violations and report them to Program Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations include: over 8 pages (not including references); double submission as per policy; supplementary material includes a newer version of the paper; plagiarism. Specify exact nature of any violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarize with CMT review fields and interface
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'Detailed Reviews and Discussions' area and understand the review form and table entries in CMT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download assigned papers via 'Download Assigned Papers' (zip). Learn sorting, abstracts toggles, and how to add or edit reviews. Ensure browser supports cookies/JS and add the conference email to safe senders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete review form and assign preliminary rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter a preliminary rating using the review form; the form contains detailed instructions about writing the review and meanings of different ratings (Oral, Poster, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save drafts if needed; drafts are visible only to you. 'Submit' makes the review visible to the Area Chair and requires all required items to be filled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use offline review/upload features correctly (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may optionally download review stubs to review offline and re-upload, but must follow formatting/character restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test by downloading a template, filling it in, and uploading. Verify the review after uploading, since upload will overwrite current review. Use XML editors as suggested and avoid prohibited characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in post-rebuttal discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: After the rebuttal period, reviewers should work with Area Chairs to clear up confusions and attempt to reach consensus on papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CMT bulletin board for anonymous AC notes; reviewers will be notified and asked to respond. Reviewers' identities are hidden from each other in that discussion feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final recommendation should reflect full context
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter a final recommendation after rebuttal that may differ from the preliminary rating and should reflect all other reviews, the authors' rebuttal, and discussion about the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider new information but follow rebuttal limitations (do not give weight to new experimental results).

rubrics_metrics.name: No required minimum acceptance/rejection quota
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no minimum number of papers a reviewer should accept or reject; evaluate each paper on its own merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe most of your assigned papers have value, accept them. If you believe most are poor, provide clear and specific comments for each rejection. Do NOT assume your personal stack should mirror the overall conference acceptance rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual/double submission policy and publication definition
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting to CVPR, authors acknowledge the manuscript has not been previously published or accepted in substantially similar form in any peer-reviewed venue, nor will be submitted elsewhere during the review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this policy, 'publication' means a written work longer than four pages that was submitted for peer review and accepted after review. ArXiv and technical reports without peer review are NOT considered publications. Workshop papers (>4 pages) that were peer-reviewed DO count. Submissions should not have substantial overlap with prior publications or concurrent submissions; rule of thumb: no more than 20% overlap. Contact Program Chairs for borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspected plagiarism should be referred to the IEEE Intellectual Property office which handles plagiarism cases and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can usually recognize plagiarism; refer suspected cases to the IEEE IP office and specify concerns. Information on procedures and levels of plagiarism is available at the referenced webpage.
